mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals a weakening labor market that triggers equity sell-offs due to reduced consumer spending, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0, or the t-statistic for the return difference from baseline is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the product of HOUST and RSAFS, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending slowdown in manufacturing, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors price in reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines in late-cycle expansions are associated with positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the regime-specific Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) level below 1200.0 thousand units indicates a cooling residential market, reducing consumer confidence and corporate capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST < 1200.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a policy response to inflation, which typically precedes equity market weakness due to rising real rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (CPIAUCSL * FEDFUNDS) has a positive coefficient in a regression of 20-day returns, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) consistently signals a weakening manufacturing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings face headwinds.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.5, or the t-statistic for the return difference is not significant (p > 0.05).
